title: The Most-Searched Gen Alpha Slang of 2026
paragraphs: Do you understand what young people are saying? If not, you are not alone. Many adults are searching online to learn the meaning of new slang used by Gen Alpha, the generation born between 2010 and 2024.
A study by the website Unscramblerer looked at Google search data from January 1 to August 27, 2026. It found the Gen Alpha slang terms that people searched for most often.
The top term was "6-7." This expression does not have a clear meaning, and young people often shout it while making funny hand movements. It was chosen as Dictionary.com's Word of the Year for 2025.
The second most searched term was "chud," an insult that means something like "fool" or "jerk." In third place was "rizz," which means charm, especially the ability to attract a romantic partner.

Other popular terms included "cap" and "no cap." "Cap" means a lie, so "no cap" means "I'm not lying." Another term, "mogging," means being better than someone else in some way, such as in looks or performance.

Some terms are about how cool people are. "Aura" means coolness or charisma, and people can gain "aura points" by doing cool things. Another term, "crash out," means to suddenly lose control or have an angry or emotional breakdown. "Glazing" means praising someone too much in a way that is not sincere.

Some slang words have even entered the mainstream. For example, "maxxing," which means improving something as much as possible, was also on the list, and it was later named Dictionary.com's Word of the Year for 2026. Another term, "unc," short for "uncle," is used to call someone old.

However, adults should be careful before using these words themselves. Some of the terms on the list can be rude or offensive. For example, "bop" and "huzz" can be insulting to women, and some other words on the list come from online communities that are hostile to women.
